reason: The cited evidence directly supports the formation of TiB2, grain refinement, increased hardness, and improved wear resistance with boron addition. It also shows enhanced passive film stability and corrosion resistance at low boron content. However, the evidence does not explicitly demonstrate that the improved corrosion resistance is due to the refined microstructure and dispersed TiB2 promoting a stable passive film under simultaneous wear and corrosion, nor does it show a synergistic reduction in both wear and corrosion under coupled conditions.
premises: Boron addition to AlCoCrFeNiMo-based HEAs promotes in situ formation of TiB2 particles and refines the BCC phase.
The refined microstructure with TiB2 particles increases microhardness and wear resistance.
At low boron content (x=0.5), the stability of the passive film and corrosion resistance are enhanced.
Finer phase structures and uniformly distributed hard phases (σ-phase, TiB2) synergistically improve wear resistance.
A stable, thicker oxide film on the worn surface reduces adhesive wear.
